model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on tangible common equity

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not equity shares. Fully diluted equity shares 15,442.3m = 15,393.4m issued at 2026-03-31 (20-F balance sheet, post 1:1 bonus of 28-Aug-2025) + 48.9m treasury-method dilution (FY26 diluted weighted 15,406.4m less basic 15,357.5m, 20-F note 31), divided by 3 because 1 ADS = 3 equity shares (20-F Item 9/12: 'One ADS continues to represent three equity shares'; bonus shares were distributed to ADS holders as additional ADSs, ratio unchanged). Held flat: SBC (ESOS/RSU) is expensed inside the flow, so option exercises (~64-110m shares/yr) are not also modelled as dilution. Treasury stock (Rs 16.9bn at cost, inherited from the HDFC Ltd merger) is immaterial and ignored.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based compensation expense' Rs 22,168.7m (FY25 24,633.9m, FY24 20,115.8m). Indian ESOS/RSU settle in new shares; no net-share-settlement tax withholding line exists.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2026 net income to HDFC Bank shareholders (Rs 704,793.4m, after SBC and after NCI) less the tangible-equity retention needed to fund FY26 revenue growth of 6.3% at the current tangible-common-equity/revenue ratio of 2.229 (2.229 x Rs 137,217m revenue increase = Rs 305.9bn) = Rs 398.9bn. reported_fcf adds SBC back (street basis). Interest income is the bank's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts INR (model) to USD (quote): 1/96.30 = 0.0103842, Yahoo Finance INR=X 96.30 at 2026-10-03T03:30Z (52-week range 85.86-97.05; the 20-F convenience rate at 2026-03-31 was ~93.83). Per-share values are computed per ADS-equivalent (3 equity shares), so intrinsic_value is USD per HDB ADS and directly comparable to current_price. The build's *_inr twins (intrinsic_value_inr, weighted_iv_inr) are INR per ADS-equivalent (3 shares); INR per equity share = *_inr / 3 = USD-per-ADS x 96.30 / 3 (base Rs ~508, weighted Rs ~513 per share vs NSE Rs 721.20). Parity check: NSE HDFCBANK.NS close Rs 721.20 on 2026-10-01 (2-Oct was the Gandhi Jayanti market holiday) x 3 / 96.30 = US$22.47 per ADS, versus the HDB close at price_as_of: ADR at a ~0.6% discount to local, confirming the 1:3 ratio (a 1:2 ratio would imply US$14.98). HDB_Analysis.json states 1 ADS = 2 shares; that is wrong for the current ADS and should be corrected there.
inputs.currency_caveat: core_metrics.currency and HDB_Metrics.csv label every period 'USD'. That is a known scripts/build_facts_xbrl.py bug: HDFC Bank dual-tags its SEC XBRL in INR (the filing currency) and a USD convenience translation, and the script hardcodes currency=USD whatever unit it pulled. The stored values are INR millions (e.g. FY2025 revenue 2,190,128.1 = Rs 2,190,128.1m per the 20-F income statement; the USD convenience figure would be ~25.6bn). This DCF uses INR throughout, read directly off the FY2026 20-F statements, and converts to USD only at the per-ADS output via fx_rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity 12.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights). Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% (mature-market ~4.3% plus India country premium) = ~12.3-12.6%. Matches the 12-13% CoE range Indian brokers apply to large private banks. Discounting INR flows at a USD rate would understate the discount rate by the ~3pp INR/USD inflation differential.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: rent sits inside premises and equipment expense, i.e. inside pre-tax income. No separate lease line; lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow. NCI (HDFC Life ~49.5% minority, HDB Financial Services post-IPO minority, HDFC ERGO) took Rs 22,303m of FY26 net income; the 'ebitda' line removes its pre-tax equivalent (22,303 / (1-0.2257) = Rs 28,804m) so the flow is income to HDFC Bank common. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (USB, WFC, TFC, NTRS, NAB.AX). Engine mapping: revenue = US GAAP 'Total revenue, net' (net interest revenue + non-interest revenue incl. insurance premium; FY26 Rs 2,327,345.3m). 'ebitda' = income before tax (Rs 939,027.9m, after provisions, D&A, intangible amortisation and the policyholder-surplus transfer) + SBC (22,168.7) - pre-tax-equivalent NCI (28,804) = Rs 932,392m = 40.06% of revenue. sbc_pct 0.95%. da_pct 0 (bank D&A is an operating expense already inside pre-tax; branch/IT capex is treated as maintenance funded within it). cash tax 22.6% FY26 effective (cash taxes paid 223,557m = 23.8% of pre-tax) -> 23.0% forward. 'capex' = equity retention required to grow the balance sheet = TCE/revenue (2.229) x g/(1+g): tangible common equity Rs 5,187,687m = HDFC Bank shareholders' equity 8,167,395.6 - goodwill 1,629,510.3 - intangibles 1,350,198.4 (the HDFC Ltd merger was booked at fair value under US GAAP, so 2.98trn of acquired goodwill/intangibles carries no regulatory capital and earns nothing to retain against). Holding TCE/revenue constant keeps CET1 near today's 17.3% (minimum 8.4% incl. D-SIB surcharge); no excess capital is released to the bridge. FY0 check: (40.06-0.95)% x (1-0.2257) x 2,327,345 = Rs 704.8bn = reported NI to HDFC Bank. net_debt = 0: deposits (Rs 31.0trn) and long-term borrowings (Rs 5.1trn) are operating funding of a bank; interest on them is already in the flow. Acquired-intangible amortisation (Rs 20.7bn) is left in the flow as a cost (conservative, ~2% of NI). Anchors: FY2026 20-F (fiscal year to 2026-03-31, filed July 2026). Q1 FY2027 (Jun-26) 6-K is not in Extracted/; its NII +6.7%, NI +5%, NIM 3.26%, CASA 32% (via HDB_Analysis.json) inform the year-1 growth and margin judgment only. band_position is not meaningful here: SBC is ~1% of revenue so the house/street band is only ~US$1 wide and the price sits far above both ends (reported value ~650% = price beyond the street edge, not a market-implied SBC view). Required-return table reading: even at a 9% INR cost of equity the base path (cap-bound at 18x) gives ~US$21, so the price discounts either a sub-9% INR CoE or a path closer to the bull case. No buybacks (Indian banks do not repurchase; dividends Rs 219.1bn paid FY26, Rs 13.00/share final recommended).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: tangible_bvps_5yr_cagr (FY2021 Rs 195.8 bonus-adjusted -> FY2026 Rs 337.0 per share)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and equity CAGRs are inflated by the July-2023 reverse merger with HDFC Ltd (3.89bn shares issued, Rs 4.24trn equity incl. NCI) and by insurance-premium consolidation of HDFC Life from FY2024; they do not describe organic growth. EPS 3yr CAGR of 1.0% is depressed by the same merger (share count +36%). Per-share EPS in the CSV is pre-bonus for FY2025 and earlier (90.01 FY25 = Rs 45.01 post-bonus); CAGRs here are bonus-adjusted. Tangible BVPS 5yr CAGR (11.5%) is the cleanest organic compounding anchor and agrees with FY26 advances growth of ~12%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computed: reported operating cash flow and FCF of a bank are dominated by deposit/loan/investment flows and are not owner earnings. FY2009-FY2025 values from HDB_Metrics.csv (INR millions despite the 'USD' label); FY2026 from the 20-F statements.

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 222.9 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (TCE/revenue 2.229 held constant).
base.narrative: Merger digestion runs to plan but slowly. FY27 revenue +8% (Q1 NII +6.7%), loan growth then re-accelerates to system-plus 12% as the credit-deposit ratio normalises and PSL compliance completes. Pre-tax-to-common margin edges from 40.1% to 42% as HDFC-era borrowings (long-term debt already down 5.87trn -> 5.12trn in FY26) roll off and NIM recovers part-way (3.3% -> ~3.5%), not to the pre-merger 4%+. ROTE ~14-15%. Growth fades to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR in perpetuity (below India nominal GDP).

bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 210.0 x g/(1+g): CET1 allowed to drift from 17.3% toward ~16%, still double the 8.4% minimum.
bull.narrative: A well-regarded CEO successor clears RBI quickly, CASA rebuilds from 32% toward the high-30s as ~70% of legacy HDFC Ltd mortgage customers are cross-sold into full banking relationships, and NIM recovers toward ~3.8%. Loan growth runs 13-14% (above system) for five years on India's credit-penetration runway, card/wealth/insurance fees compound, and the margin reaches 45% (ROTE ~17%, near pre-merger levels). The ICICI P/B discount closes.

bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 222.9 x g/(1+g) percent of revenue (TCE/revenue 2.229 held constant).
bear.narrative: The margin dilution is structural: the absorbed wholesale mortgage book permanently lowers asset yields, deposit competition with ICICI and SBI keeps CASA in the low 30s, and NIM drifts toward 3.1%. Leadership transition after the October-2026 CEO exit stalls execution; credit costs normalise upward from today's 1.17% GNPA as unsecured retail seasons. Loan growth 7-9% (at or below system) as the bank defends margin; pre-tax-to-common margin slides from 40% to 37% (ROTE ~12%, at the cost of equity).

scenario_narratives.base: Merger digestion runs to plan but slowly: FY27 revenue +8%, loan growth re-accelerating to ~12% as the credit-deposit ratio normalises; NIM recovers part-way (3.3% -> ~3.5%) as HDFC-era borrowings roll off, lifting the pre-tax-to-common margin from 40.1% to 42% and ROTE to ~14-15%. Growth fades to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bull: Smooth CEO succession, CASA rebuilt toward the high-30s through cross-sell into legacy HDFC Ltd mortgage customers, NIM back toward ~3.8%; 13-14% loan growth for five years on India's credit-penetration runway, margin to 45% (ROTE ~17%) and CET1 run down modestly from 17.3% toward 16%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Margin dilution proves structural (wholesale mortgage book, low-30s CASA, deposit war with ICICI/SBI), NIM drifts to ~3.1%, leadership transition stalls execution and credit costs normalise upward; loan growth 7-9% and margin slides to 37%, ROTE ~12%, roughly equal to the cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: management's 'coming quarters' NIM/CASA recovery has slipped for three years and Q1 FY27 NIM (3.26%) was the post-merger low, and the CEO departs 26-Oct-2026 with the RBI-approved successor not yet named. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (successor, CASA rebuild, NIM recovery, above-system growth). Base 50%: asset quality is clean (GNPA 1.17%), capital is ample (CET1 17.3%), and the franchise is not impaired.

entry_price.hurdle_note: 15% is applied to INR flows. With INR depreciating ~3%/yr against USD over the long run, a 15% INR IRR is roughly a 12% USD IRR for an ADR holder.

valuation_philosophy.summary: HDFC Bank is valued as a bank: free cash flow to equity (net income to common less the tangible equity retained to fund balance-sheet growth at today's capital ratio) discounted at a 12.5% INR cost of equity, with deposits and borrowings treated as operating funding (net debt = 0). The judgment that matters is ROTE versus cost of equity versus growth: at ~14% ROTE, 12.5% CoE and ~12% growth, almost all value comes from the long growth runway, so the terminal growth and margin-recovery paths dominate. US GAAP tangible equity strips the Rs 2.98trn of merger goodwill and intangibles; at the current price the bank trades at ~2.1x that tangible book.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM/CASA recovery: each 1pp of pre-tax-to-common margin is ~2.5% of value; the bear path assumes the HDFC Ltd margin dilution is permanent.
CEO succession: Sashidhar Jagdishan retires 26-Oct-2026; the successor needs RBI approval.
Cost of equity and terminal growth in INR: the valuation is long-duration (growth near CoE for five years); see the sensitivity grid.
INR/USD: values are converted at spot; continued rupee depreciation lowers the USD value of an ADS independent of operations.
Capital: retention holds CET1 near 17.3%; an RBI tightening (expected-credit-loss transition, risk-weight changes on unsecured retail) would raise retention and lower FCFE.
Data: core_metrics/CSV mislabel INR as USD (build_facts_xbrl.py bug); HDB_Analysis.json mis-states the ADS ratio as 1:2 (it is 1:3).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for HDB at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 21.77-37.45. Local cross-check HDFCBANK.NS (52-week range Rs 681.9-1,020.5) and INR=X from the same API; see inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: HDFC Bank 20-F for fiscal 2026 (year to 2026-03-31, auditor's report 29-Jul-2026): consolidated balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, shareholders' equity and note 31 (EPS) read directly in INR millions from research/HDB/Extracted/HDB_20F_FY2026.txt. History FY2008-FY2025 from HDB_Metrics.csv / core_metrics, whose currency column wrongly says USD: the values are INR millions (build_facts_xbrl.py hardcodes USD for dual-tagged INR/USD XBRL filers; same bug as BILI). See inputs.currency_caveat.
data_sources.qualitative: HDB_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q1 FY2027 results, CEO succession, NIM/CASA trend, guidance.
